java_locations.role: Obtains the complete Java2D glyph outline as a PathIterator and delegates every path segment to SvgGraphics.
Maps every PathIterator.SEG_CLOSE to a literal SVG Z command before filling the glyph path.

rust_locations.role: Converts ab_glyph outline curves to SVG commands but emits Z only when ab_glyph supplies an explicit closing line whose endpoint equals the contour start.

claimed_invariant: Every filled glyph contour produced by Java TextLayout.getOutline is closed by one PathIterator.SEG_CLOSE, and SvgGraphics preserves it as one Z command. TrueType contours are implicitly closed even when a font decoder's curve inventory omits a final line back to the start. Therefore each Rust contour move must terminate with exactly one Z regardless of whether ab_glyph exposes that implicit edge.
causal_divergence: The Rust converter infers closure only from an explicit line ending at contour_start. The embedded TrueType outlines for G and U end their final visible curve away from the first point because the font format supplies closure implicitly; ab_glyph does not add a synthetic closing line. Rust consequently emits paths whose numeric commands now match Java exactly but lack Java's final Z.
planned_model_change: Treat transitions between ab_glyph contour starts and exhaustion of the final curve list as contour boundaries. Emit Z for the preceding open contour at each boundary and after the final curve. Retain the existing explicit-close handling so contours that already return to their start receive no duplicate Z. Do not inspect the character, fixture, path coordinates, or command count.

checked_derivations.derivation: After the measured-header centering fix, every M/L/Q coordinate is byte-identical and the sole residual is Java's trailing `Z `.
After the same independent centering fix, every numeric path coordinate is byte-identical and the sole residual is Java's trailing `Z `.

perturbation_axes: uppercase, lowercase, and numeric spot characters
shifted positive and negative glyph centers
scope_boundary: This mechanism owns only the preservation of implicit filled-contour closure while converting embedded-font outlines to SVG. It does not own glyph metrics, glyph centers, class header placement, SVEK entity coordinates, fill rules, comparator behavior, or corpus eligibility.
acceptance: Every generated contour has exactly one M and one Z across fresh single-contour and multi-contour characters.
G and U evidence paths become byte-identical without character-specific logic.
Existing characters whose contours already expose an explicit closing line do not acquire duplicate Z commands.
The full no-oracle ratchet does not regress any family.
Renderer tests, clippy, and the four frozen mechanical guards pass except for explicitly pre-existing gate debt.
An independent checker records a verdict and held-out Java/Rust evidence at the exact implementation revision.

experimental_result.result: Generic contour-boundary closure makes all four affected spot-character diagrams structurally equivalent: class_spot_letter_G, class_spot_letter_U, edge_class_spots, and edge_stereotype_spot_colors.
experimental_result.headline_effect: No-oracle product parity increases from 11149/11251 to 11153/11251: class 1964/1971 to 1966/1971 and edge-cases 748/777 to 750/777.
experimental_result.counterexample_that_shaped_the_change: The first endpoint-based implementation failed the fresh digit 8 perturbation because its quadratic contours already returned geometrically to their starts but still required distinct Java SEG_CLOSE commands. The final implementation tracks emitted closure semantics instead of endpoint equality.
